pages.title: About Cole
pages.html:
Cole Howey

Analytics and decision science leader: experimentation, causal inference and applied machine learning for operational decisions.

Cole is Sr. Manager of Data Analytics—Operations at Dick's Sporting Goods, where he leads the analytics team that serves Operations, Technology and Finance. He designs A/B tests, builds causal models and applies machine learning so that leaders can decide what to roll out, what to stop and why a metric moved.

He also defines and governs the metrics and data those decisions depend on. He has designed new operational metrics, co-led an enterprise inventory data model, and worked with data engineering on table schemas, event instrumentation and governed tables on Azure Databricks.

Background in brief

  • Sr. Manager of Data Analytics—Operations, Dick's Sporting Goods (October 2024 – present)
  • Sr. Manager of Strategy, Executive Development Program, Dick's Sporting Goods (September 2023 – October 2024)
  • MBA Associate, Commercial Analytics & Supply Chain Operations, Taiho Oncology (May – August 2022)
  • Assistant Program Manager, Lockheed Martin (part time, during his undergraduate degree)
  • U.S. Air Force, active duty (August 2012 – December 2017), then Air National Guard (through May 2020)

Education

  • MS, Applied Data Science, University of Chicago (part time, started Autumn 2026, expected March 2028)
  • MBA, Business Analytics Track, Carnegie Mellon University, Tepper School of Business (May 2023)
  • BS, Civil Engineering, University of Central Florida (May 2021)

Skills

  • Experimentation: A/B test design, minimum detectable effect simulation, sensitivity analysis with confidence intervals.
  • Statistical and causal modeling: fixed-effects regression, generalized linear models (including Gamma GLMs with interaction terms), linear models, hypothesis testing.
  • Machine learning: principal component analysis (PCA) and K-means clustering for store segmentation; supervised methods through coursework. Machine Learning I and II are scheduled for Winter and Spring 2027.
  • SQL: used throughout his career on Google BigQuery and Databricks SQL, for experiment data, customer cohorts, reporting and schema design.
  • R: the language Cole uses most for statistical modeling and experiment analysis.
  • Python: the primary language of most courses in his MS in Applied Data Science, and the language of his team's store segmentation pipeline at Dick's Sporting Goods. He also used Python in MBA coursework.
  • Data platforms: Azure Databricks, Google BigQuery, metric and schema design, event-flag design, Git and GitHub.
  • Business intelligence: Power BI (enterprise reporting), Tableau.
  • Generative AI evaluation: validating LLM-generated SQL against governed reports in Databricks Genie Spaces.
  • Leadership: hiring, coaching and growing an analytics team; presenting to executives; project and program management.

Based in

Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

pages.title: University of Chicago — MS in Applied Data Science
pages.html:
University of Chicago

MS, Applied Data Science (started Autumn 2026, expected March 2028)

Cole is completing the degree part time, two courses per quarter, while working full time. Most courses are taught in Python.

Course plan

The program has six core courses, a two-quarter capstone and four electives.

  • Autumn 2026 (September – December 2026): Statistical Models for Data Science; Leadership & Consulting for Data Science
  • Winter 2027 (January – March 2027): Time Series Analysis and Forecasting; Machine Learning I
  • Spring 2027 (March – June 2027): Machine Learning II; Cloud-Native Data Engineering
  • Summer 2027 (June – August 2027): two electives. Planned: Causal Models for Data Science; Bayesian Machine Learning with GenAI Applications
  • Autumn 2027 (September – December 2027): Capstone I; one elective. Planned: Machine Learning Operations
  • Winter 2028 (January – March 2028): Capstone II; one elective. Planned: Applied Gen AI: Agents & Multimodal Intelligence

The elective choices are Cole's current plan. Elective offerings vary by quarter, so the plan can change.

Course projects will be added to the Projects page as they are completed.

pages.title: Dick's Sporting Goods — Sr. Manager of Data Analytics—Operations
pages.html:
Dick's Sporting Goods

Sr. Manager of Data Analytics—Operations (October 2024 – present)

Cole leads the analytics team that acts as internal consultants to Operations, Technology and Finance. The work covers store operations, online order fulfillment from stores, and the supply chain from distribution centers to stores. He grew the team from one analyst to five, wrote the hiring documentation, and coaches analysts on methods and stakeholder communication.

Experimentation
  • Designs A/B tests of operational processes across the store fleet.
  • Simulates the minimum detectable effect before a test starts, and builds sensitivity analysis that estimates return on investment with confidence intervals.
  • Analyzes tests with fixed-effects regression in R.
  • Test results have informed leadership decisions on whether to roll out an initiative, including decisions not to roll out initiatives that did not show a positive return.
Causal modeling and root-cause analysis
  • Builds generalized linear models, including Gamma GLMs with interaction terms, to explain why an operational or ecommerce metric changed when a controlled test is not possible.
  • This work has identified the date a metric shifted and the cause behind it, which allowed the responsible team to correct it.
Machine learning
  • Cole built the team's first store segmentation with principal component analysis (PCA) and K-means clustering in R.
  • An analyst on his team later rebuilt it in Python to run on Databricks, with the code versioned in GitHub.
  • The segmentation replaced manual, subjective store classification and is used across several store-tiering decisions.
Metric and data governance
  • Designed a new units-per-hour (UPH) productivity metric for ship-from-store fulfillment. His team analyzed timestamp data to derive the event flags the metric needs, software engineers built those flags into the fulfillment product, and Cole's team directed the data cleaning.
  • Partnered with Data Engineering on the event services that deliver this data into Databricks, where it feeds governed tables for analytics and reporting.
  • Co-led an enterprise RFID inventory data model on Azure Databricks with Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering and Product Management, translating business requirements into governed metrics and reusable data products.
  • Regularly presents new metrics and data designs to senior leaders.
AI-enabled analytics
  • Represented analytics in building Databricks Genie Spaces for natural-language, self-service analytics. The company's data organization engineered the tables. Cole's team defined the business logic and trusted table joins, validated the LLM-generated SQL against governed reports, and refined each space's context to reduce incorrect answers.
  • Partnered with engineering on a demonstration to senior executives.
Business intelligence
  • Stood up enterprise Power BI reporting that gives field leaders across more than 700 stores a consolidated view of their goal metrics.
  • Replaced manual Excel executive reports with automated Power BI reports.
Tools

SQL, R, Python, Azure Databricks, Google BigQuery, Power BI, GitHub.

pages.title: Dick's Sporting Goods — Sr. Manager of Strategy, Executive Development Program
pages.html:
Sr. Manager of Strategy, Executive Development Program (September 2023 – October 2024)

Cole joined Dick's Sporting Goods through its Executive Development Program, a rotational leadership program for MBA graduates housed in the Strategy department. The projects were strategy-oriented: market sizing, idea generation and business case development.

  • Marketing Personalization rotation: ran A/B tests on direct marketing channels: SMS, push notifications and email.
  • Loss Prevention rotation: coordinated a multi-tactic pilot across operations, finance, analytics and loss prevention, tracked deployment against the measurement plan, and informed the rollout strategy.
  • Opportunity sizing: built a SQL cohort analysis that measured customer spend relative to the date customers adopted a service, then proposed and won support for adding the opportunity to the Technology roadmap.

Taiho Oncology

MBA Associate, Commercial Analytics & Supply Chain Operations (May – August 2022, Princeton, NJ)

  • Executive analytics: served as an internal consultant on a CEO-directed project. Ran A/B tests and built interaction and linear models in R to measure the effect of sales representatives on monthly sales, then presented recommendations to the executive team.
  • Data modeling: replaced a legacy Excel supply chain system with a SQL entity-relationship model of more than 200,000 entities, normalized and with data governance protocols. This cut weekly data preparation time by 90%.

  • Dashboards: built web-based supply chain dashboards for commercial leaders that tracked channel health, product-level sales, and distributor inventory and sell-through.

  • Ran project tracking and status reporting for a cross-functional program.

pages.title: U.S. Air Force and Air National Guard
pages.html:
U.S. Air Force

Active duty (August 2012 – December 2017)

Cole enlisted at 18 and served about five and a half years on active duty in structural maintenance, a construction trade. He separated as a Staff Sergeant.

  • Did hands-on construction and facilities work at Eielson Air Force Base (Alaska), Daegu (South Korea) and Malmstrom Air Force Base (Montana).
  • Earned an early promotion at 21, three years ahead of schedule.
  • Moved into construction project management for about the last two years of his enlistment. He managed projects from scoping and scheduling through crew coordination and completion, on an indefinite-delivery contract.
  • Directly managed two Airmen for about a year and a half.

Air National Guard (through May 2020)

Cole continued to serve in the Air National Guard while he completed his civil engineering degree and worked part time at Lockheed Martin.
